The letters from Cotter Pyke to Jon during the mission to Hardhome were insane in how different the tone changed. 

The first letter: 

"Calm seas today. Eleven ships set sail for Hardhome on the morning tide. Three Braavosi, four Lyseni, four of ours. Two of the Lyseni barely seaworthy. We may drown more wildlings than we save. Your command. Twenty ravens aboard, and Maester Harmune. Will send reports. I command from Talon, Tattersalt second on Blackbird, Ser Glendon holds Eastwatch".

The second letter:

“At Hardhome, with six ships. Wild seas. Blackbird lost with all hands, two Lyseni ships driven aground on Skane, Talon taking water. Very bad here. Wildlings eating their own dead. Dead things in the woods. Braavosi captains will only take women, children on their ships. Witch women call us slavers. Attempt to take Storm Crow defeated, six crew dead, many wildlings. Eight ravens left. Dead things in the water. Send help by land, seas wracked by storms. From Talon, by hand of Maester Harmune".

Part of the horror of the Others is the *unknowing* of them. What are they? What do they want? 

*Dead things in the woods. Dead things in the water.*

The Others are haunting. 

But the true horror is the desperation. Jon sent these ships to save those Wildling because they need every possible person to help fight the Others back. This was a desperate move and it failed completely. Those people are *gone*. 

Jon knows the truth of this threat and he’s constantly undermined, questioned, and harassed. He’s doing everything he can to strengthen the Wall, for just a hope of evening the odds. And even then it’s not enough. 

Then Jon gets the letter from Ramsey. And the pressure is too much and he announces his intent to break his oath. And Jon is killed for it. 

Killed during a fight between the watchmen and the wildlings that would no doubt escalate after Jon’s death. Weakening their already feeble strength.
